question.text: Ekanta Mid-Market Fund issues two classes of units: Class A (retail LPs, ticket <INR 10 cr) and Class B (institutional LPs, ticket >INR 100 cr). Per Chapter 6, it is permissible and common for the FUND to:

answer.text: Charge a higher mgmt fee to Class B to reflect relationship premium
Offer different management-fee and carry rates across classes (Class B typically lower) as captured in the PPM's class-wise economics
Commingle classes' economics — no class distinction is permitted
Give Class A a fee waiver and Class B a fee premium

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 6: 'fees may vary depending on the amount the investor commits and timelines of commitment; these are usually captured as fees in different classes of units issued by the fund.' Larger/earlier commitments typically get FEE DISCOUNTS (lower mgmt fee and/or carry), not premiums. The Trap: A reverses the direction; C is false; D reverses the logic. Cross-Exam Context: Same in XIX-C. SEBI permits class-based differentiation as long as disclosed in the PPM; fair-allocation obligations apply. Manager's Pro-Tip: Document class economics meticulously: Class A 2%/20%, Class B 1.75%/18%, Anchor 1.5%/15%, etc. At first close, anchor discount can be material — but you must offer it to ALL similarly-placed anchors or you breach the fair-allocation duty.
